records.central_bank: Centrale Bank van Curaçao en Sint Maarten
records.people: José Jardim (member of the Board of Directors / Financial Economic Director, CBCS, 2017 to 30 June 2025)
records.move: from Financial Economic Director and board member of the Centrale Bank van Curaçao en Sint Maarten to Chief Executive Officer of Banco di Caribe (effective 1 July 2025)
records.summary: The Curaçao Chronicle reports that Jardim, a CBCS board member since 2017 responsible for financial and economic supervision and monetary policy, became CEO of the commercial bank Banco di Caribe effective 1 July, ending an eight-year tenure at the central bank. The same report settles the ownership of the employer: Banco di Caribe has been wholly owned by United Group Holdings, a privately held group headed by Curaçao businessman Gregory Elias, since 2022. The CBCS Supervisory Board's own announcement of his departure effective 30 June 2025 states only that he would assume a leadership position at a commercial bank, without naming it.
records.source_title: José Jardim appointed new CEO of Banco di Caribe (Curaçao Chronicle)
records.quote: Jardim's appointment marks the end of his eight-year tenure at CBCS, where he has been a board member since 2017.
records.second_source_title: Announcement of the Supervisory Board on the departure of Financial Economic Director Mr. Jose Jardim PhD as of June 30, 2025 (Curaçao Chronicle)
records.second_source_quote: assume a leadership position at a commercial bank

records.people: Mr O. 'Nete (non-executive director, Central Bank of Lesotho board)
records.move: from senior finance and credit manager at Standard Bank of Lesotho, and Tax Manager at STANLIB, to non-executive director of the Central Bank of Lesotho
records.summary: The Central Bank of Lesotho's own board page gives non-executive director Mr O. 'Nete's career, which includes a senior finance and credit management post at the Standard Bank of Lesotho and a tax manager post at STANLIB; the page gives no dates for those posts. Ownership of the employer is stated on Standard Bank Group's own group-structure page, which lists Standard Lesotho Bank Limited at 80% among the group's companies, the group itself being a privately held, stock-exchange-listed banking group; the same page lists STANLIB's parent Liberty Holdings Limited as a group subsidiary under the note that holdings in subsidiaries are 100% unless otherwise indicated.

records.people: Mohamed Lamine Lebbou (Governor of the Banque d'Algérie, appointed February 2026)
records.move: from BNP Paribas El Djazaïr (2004-2006) to Governor of the Banque d'Algérie (February 2026), after heading the state-owned Banque nationale d'Algérie 2021-2024 and BEA International Bank from May 2025
records.summary: TSA Algerie's profile of the new governor states that his career began at BNP Paribas El Djazair from 2004 to 2006, before university teaching, company posts and the state-owned Banque nationale d'Algerie, which he headed from 2021 to 2024, and BEA International Bank, the French subsidiary of the state Banque exterieure d'Algerie, from May 2025. The private ownership of the first employer is stated in BNP Paribas El Djazair's own 2018 annual report, which says the bank is 100% owned by BNP Paribas France; the later banking posts named are state-owned and are not counted as private moves.

records.people: Mrs M. Mohasoa (non-executive director, Central Bank of Lesotho board)
records.move: from member of the board and chairman of the audit and risk committee of Liberty Life Lesotho (2017 to 2021) to non-executive director of the Central Bank of Lesotho
records.summary: The Central Bank of Lesotho's own board page states that non-executive director Mrs M. Mohasoa was a member of the board and chairman of the audit and risk committee of the insurer Liberty Life Lesotho from 2017 to 2021. Ownership is stated in two further pages: the South African Reserve Bank's list of designated entities names Liberty Life Lesotho Ltd within the Liberty Insurance Group, and Liberty Holdings' own 2019 annual report states that Standard Bank Group Limited holds a 53.6% interest in Liberty's issued ordinary share capital, Standard Bank Group being a stock-exchange-listed private banking group.
records.source_title: Board of Directors (Central Bank of Lesotho)
records.quote: Member of the Board and the Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee of Liberty Life Lesotho from 2017 to 2021.
records.second_source_quote: 53,6% (2018: 53,6%) interest in the issued ordinary share capital of Liberty

records.people: Jaime Valencia Valencia (General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia 1996-2006 and again from 16 January 2020; Manager of International Operations 1994-1996)
records.move: from senior posts at Banco de la Unión S.A., Banco de Cochabamba S.A. and Compañía Boliviana de Seguros S.A. to General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia
records.summary: The Banco Central de Bolivia's own CV for its General Manager states that he held the post from 1996 to 2006 and again from 16 January 2020, and was the bank's Manager of International Operations from 1994 to 1996, and that he held important positions at Banco de la Union S.A., Banco de Cochabamba S.A. and Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. The CV gives no job titles and no dates for those three firms, and no source opened this round states the ownership of any of them, so the move is filed uncounted pending an ownership check. The regulator ASFI's own history of financial supervision, which would settle how Banco de Cochabamba was owned, returned a client error and needs a hand check; a Los Tiempos anniversary article on the insurer's successor company names no shareholders.
records.source_title: Currículum: Jaime Valencia Valencia, Gerente General (Banco Central de Bolivia)
records.quote: Banco de la Unión S.A.; Banco de Cochabamba S.A.; Compañía Boliviana de Seguros

records.people: George Manuel Hazoury (member of the Junta Monetaria of the Banco Central de la República Dominicana until his replacement under decree 532-20 in 2020)
records.move: from administrator of Banco de Reservas to member of the Junta Monetaria of the Banco Central de la República Dominicana
records.summary: El Dinero's report on decree 532-20, which named the economists Arturo Martinez Moya and Eduardo Tejera to the Junta Monetaria for two years, states that the outgoing members they replaced were Manuel Garcia Arevalo, a former Minister of Industry and Commerce, and George Manuel Hazoury, who had been administrator of Banco de Reservas. The page does not state who owns Banco de Reservas; it is the Dominican state's own bank by name, so the record is filed as a public-sector move and is not counted. The report gives no career details for the two incoming members.
records.source_title: Designan a Martínez Moya y Eduardo Tejera en la Junta Monetaria (elDinero)
